taxonomic_note: Preserve species-level source concept; no subspecies assigned. The source photograph uses a nominate horticultural label; that does not determine the user's source row below species.
look_here_first: Start with the broad, fleshy, toothed leaves and terminal spine. Compare mature leaf width and the flowering architecture: a branched panicle supports A. americana, while lechuguilla has narrower leaves and a largely spike-like flowering axis.

best_field_traits: Broad fleshy rosette leaves, typically (80–)100–200 cm long in the existing FNA-based review.
Marginal teeth about 5–10 mm; a strong terminal spine.
Flowering axis branches into a panicle, unlike the largely spicate lechuguilla axis.
morphology_keys.leaves: Mature broad succulent leaves; tooth and terminal spine characters should be inspected at close range with scale.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Branched flowering panicle; full flowering-axis photo still needed.
morphology_keys.lookalike_separators: A. lechuguilla: much narrower leaves, typically 30–50 × 2–4(–5.2) cm, and largely spicate inflorescence. Do not diagnose species or local nativity by blue color, variegation, or ornamental occurrence. Other cultivated agaves can overlap; require reproductive/leaf-edge evidence when uncertain.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas native at state level in POWO; local origin/cultivation and >=3 target-county native certification remain UNRESOLVED.

curation_status.review_basis: Existing Master Plant Pool scientific review; exact accepted-name verification repeated 2026-10-14

diagnostic_photo_plan: Leaf teeth and terminal spine macro with ruler

source_pool_review.taxonomy_review: Reviewed 2026-10-09 — accepted Agave americana L. (POWO/WCVP); Texas native at STATE level, but project target-county status UNRESOLVED and cultivated/local-origin ambiguity remains. Kew accepts multiple infraspecifics including subsp. americana and subsp. protamericana; source species row does not certify one. Preserve approved source-pool learner admission. No three-county PASS. Sources: https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:319063-2 ; https://efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=100796
source_pool_review.curation_status_before_install: Taxonomy reviewed — approved_pending_curation; range UNRESOLVED; not canonical
source_pool_review.diagnostic_notes: LOOK HERE FIRST: mature smooth, fleshy broad leaves ca. (80-)100–200 cm, marginal teeth ca. 5–10 mm, versus A. lechuguilla narrow 30–50 × 2–4(-5.2) cm leaves. If flowering, A. americana has branching panicle, A. lechuguilla mostly spicate axis. Leaf color/variegation and ornamental occurrence do not prove species or local nativity. PHOTO ROLES: whole rosette with scale, marginal teeth + apical spine, full flowering scape, flower/ovary close-up; separate wild vouchers from horticultural cultivars.
source_pool_review.accepted_name_note: Accepted Agave americana L.; Aloe americana (L.) Crantz homotypic synonym; Agave spectabilis Salisb. illegitimate superfluous name. POWO recognizes multiple subspecies/varieties; source not resolved below species.
